intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III (HHC3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the AP2S1 gene (602242) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III (HHC3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the AP2S1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15
checks.explanation: Heterozygous AP2S1 mutations cause FHH3.

checks.claim: The AP2S1 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: An analysis of SNVs within the 3.46Mbp interval on 19q13.3, which is the location of the FHH3 locus, and contains ~110 genes, revealed one SNV, a C to T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene
checks.explanation: AP2S1 lies in the 19q13.3 interval.

paragraphs.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is an autosomal dominant disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis. It is marked by lifelong hypercalcemia with inappropriately normal or raised parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels and low urinary calcium excretion. It is genetically distinct from HHC1, which is caused by mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR). HHC3 results from mutation in the sigma-2 subunit of adaptor protein-2 (AP2S1), which takes part in clathrin-mediated endocytosis of the calcium-sensing receptor.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is an autosomal dominant disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis.
checks.evidence_quote: FHH3, together with FHH1 and FHH2 are genetically heterogenous autosomal dominant disorders of extracellular-calcium (Cao2+) homeostasis

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is characterized by lifelong hypercalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by lifelong elevations of serum calcium concentrations with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is characterized by inappropriately normal or raised parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels.
checks.evidence_quote: Serum iPTH levels, determined in three separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years in the group of 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically and appeared to increase further thereafter.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows raised iPTH in this one FBH kindred. It does not support a general description of HHC3 or the 'inappropriately normal' wording.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is characterized by low urinary calcium excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by lifelong elevations of serum calcium concentrations with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion (mean urinary calcium:creatinine clearance ratio <0.01)

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is genetically distinct from HHC1.
checks.evidence_quote: The loci for FHH1, FHH2, and FHH3 are located on chromosomes 3q21.1, 19p, and 19q13.3, respectively
checks.explanation: Different loci show that FHH3 is genetically distinct from FHH1.

checks.claim: HHC1 is caused by mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR).
checks.evidence_quote: FBHH1 is caused by mutations of a calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), but the abnormalities underlying FBHH2 and FBHH3 are unknown.
checks.explanation: The paper states that FBHH1 (HHC1) is caused by CaSR mutations.

checks.claim: HHC3 results from mutation in AP2S1, the sigma-2 subunit of adaptor protein-2.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that missense mutations of AP2 σ subunit (AP2S1) affecting Arg15 ... result in familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3 (FHH3)

checks.claim: The AP2 sigma-2 subunit (AP2S1) takes part in clathrin-mediated endocytosis of the calcium-sensing receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, our studies demonstrate that AP2σ2 has a role in CaSR endocytosis as well as in the regulation of CaSR signaling via Cai2+
checks.explanation: The paper also describes AP2 as pivotal in clathrin-mediated endocytosis.

paragraphs.text: McMurtry et al. (1992) described a large kindred from Oklahoma with familial benign hypercalcemia. Affected members had hypercalcemia, raised serum PTH, hypophosphatemia and low urinary calcium excretion, and some had features of osteomalacia. These features set the kindred apart from typical families with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, and the disorder became known as the Oklahoma variant.

checks.claim: McMurtry et al. (1992) described a large kindred from Oklahoma with familial benign hypercalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: A large kindred with familial benign hypercalcemia (FBH) is described
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a large FBH kindred but does not say it is from Oklahoma.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Oklahoma kindred had hypercalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the 46 individuals studied, 19 were found to be affected. Serum iPTH levels, determined in three separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years in the group of 15 hypercalcemic subjects
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the affected members as hypercalcemic.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Oklahoma kindred had raised serum PTH.
checks.evidence_quote: Serum iPTH levels, determined in three separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years in the group of 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically and appeared to increase further thereafter.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that serum iPTH rose above normal in affected adults.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Oklahoma kindred had hypophosphatemia.
checks.evidence_quote: inorganic phosphate levels were lower than in unaffected kindred members
checks.explanation: Phosphate was lower in affected members, and the conclusions refer to mild hypophosphatemia.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Oklahoma kindred had low urinary calcium excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone levels in a large kindred with familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcemia.
checks.explanation: The title says 'hypocalciuric', but the abstract gives no urinary calcium measurements.

checks.claim: Some affected members of the Oklahoma kindred had features of osteomalacia.
checks.evidence_quote: Three of five affected adults older than age 40 years who were studied radiographically had changes suggestive of osteomalacia.
checks.explanation: Osteomalacia features were seen in some affected adults, and a biopsy confirmed defective mineralization.

checks.claim: The features of the Oklahoma kindred distinguished it from typical families with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, and the disorder became known as the Oklahoma variant.
checks.evidence_quote: will help to clarify if we have observed an unusual variant of FBH.
checks.explanation: The authors suggest the kindred may be an unusual variant, but the abstract does not use the name 'Oklahoma variant'.

paragraphs.text: In the Oklahoma kindred, HHC3 was transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.claim: In the Oklahoma kindred, HHC3 was transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: used to demonstrate its cosegregation in members (32 affected and 23 unaffected) from 4 generations of the two kindreds
checks.explanation: The paper says FHH3 is autosomal dominant and shows cosegregation across both kindreds. It does not explicitly describe the inheritance pattern in the Oklahoma kindred alone.

paragraphs.text: Lloyd et al. (1999) used linkage analysis in the Oklahoma kindred to map the familial benign hypercalcemia Oklahoma variant to chromosome 19q13. They excluded linkage to the CASR locus on chromosome 3q and to the HHC2 locus on 19p.

checks.claim: Lloyd et al. (1999) used linkage analysis in the Oklahoma kindred to map the familial benign hypercalcemia Oklahoma variant to chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage was established between FBHOk and eight chromosome 19q13 loci, with the highest LOD score, 6.67 (recombination fraction.00), obtained with D19S606.
checks.explanation: The paper reports linkage mapping of FBHOk to 19q13 in the Oklahoma family.

checks.claim: Lloyd et al. (1999) excluded linkage of the Oklahoma variant to the CASR locus on chromosome 3q.
checks.evidence_quote: in an Oklahoma family with an FBH variant (FBHOk), for which linkage to 3q and 19p had been excluded.
checks.explanation: Linkage to 3q is described as already excluded ('had been excluded'), apparently before this study, so it is not clearly Lloyd et al.'s own finding.

checks.claim: Lloyd et al. (1999) excluded linkage of the Oklahoma variant to the HHC2 locus on chromosome 19p.
checks.evidence_quote: together with the mapping of another FBH locus to 19p13.3, suggests that additional CaSRs or second messengers may be involved. These may be identified by positional cloning, and we therefore performed a genomewide search, using chromosome-specific sets of microsatellite polymorphisms, in an Oklahoma family with an FBH variant (FBHOk), for which linkage to 3q and 19p had been excluded.
checks.explanation: Linkage to the 19p FBH locus is described as already excluded, apparently by earlier work, not shown in this study.

paragraphs.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is genetically heterogeneous. HHC1 is caused by mutation in CASR on chromosome 3q, HHC2 by mutation in GNA11 on chromosome 19p, and HHC3 by mutation in AP2S1 on chromosome 19q.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial benign hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia (FBHH) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder that consists of three designated types, FBHH1, FBHH2 and FBHH3
checks.explanation: The paper explicitly calls the disorder genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: HHC1 is caused by mutation in CASR on chromosome 3q.
checks.evidence_quote: FBHH and NSHPT in most families is caused by loss-of-function mutations of the gene encoding the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) located on chromosome 3q21.1.
checks.explanation: The paper places FBHH1 at 3q21.1 and attributes it to CaSR mutations.

checks.claim: HHC2 is caused by mutation in GNA11 on chromosome 19p.
checks.evidence_quote: The loci for FHH1, FHH2, and FHH3 are located on chromosomes 3q21.1, 19p, and 19q13.3, respectively
checks.explanation: The paper gives the FHH2 locus on 19p but does not name GNA11 as the gene.

checks.claim: HHC3 is caused by mutation in AP2S1 on chromosome 19q.
checks.evidence_quote: The loci for FHH1, FHH2, and FHH3 are located on chromosomes 3q21.1, 19p, and 19q13.3, respectively
checks.explanation: FHH3 is caused by AP2S1 mutations at 19q13.3.

paragraphs.text: Nesbit et al. (2013) studied the Oklahoma kindred and patients with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia who did not carry CASR mutations. They identified heterozygous missense mutations in the AP2S1 gene, all affecting the same residue, arg15 (R15C, R15H and R15L). In vitro, the mutations reduced the sensitivity of cells expressing the calcium-sensing receptor to extracellular calcium and reduced receptor endocytosis. These results suggested that the arg15 mutations impair AP2-mediated internalization of the calcium-sensing receptor.

checks.claim: Nesbit et al. (2013) studied the Oklahoma kindred and patients with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia who did not carry CASR mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: of the previously reported FHHOK kindred, and 23 family members (16 affected members and 7 unaffected members), from three generations, of the reported FHHNI kindred were investigated. In addition, 50 reported FHH patients (23 males and 27 females) in whom CASR mutations had not been detected

checks.claim: Nesbit et al. (2013) identified heterozygous missense mutations in the AP2S1 gene in these patients, all affecting residue arg15 (R15C, R15H, and R15L).
checks.evidence_quote: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15 and consisted of four Arg15Cys, three Arg15His, and four Arg15Leu mutations

checks.claim: In vitro, the AP2S1 arg15 mutations reduced the sensitivity of calcium-sensing receptor-expressing cells to extracellular calcium.
checks.evidence_quote: AP2S1 mutations decreased the sensitivity of CaSR-expressing cells to extracellular calcium and reduced CaSR endocytosis

checks.claim: In vitro, the AP2S1 arg15 mutations reduced calcium-sensing receptor endocytosis.
checks.evidence_quote: AP2S1 mutations decreased the sensitivity of CaSR-expressing cells to extracellular calcium and reduced CaSR endocytosis
checks.explanation: In the full text, only Arg15Cys was tested for endocytosis.

checks.claim: Nesbit et al. (2013) concluded that the AP2S1 arg15 mutations impair AP2-mediated internalization of the calcium-sensing receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, our studies demonstrate that AP2σ2 has a role in CaSR endocytosis as well as in the regulation of CaSR signaling via Cai2+ (Fig. 2), a pathway pivotal for Cao2+ homeostasis, such that its disruption by AP2S1 Arg15 mutants results in FHH3.

paragraphs.text: Later reports suggested that patients with AP2S1 mutations may have higher serum calcium levels and lower urinary calcium excretion than patients with HHC1, and some have had cognitive or developmental problems. The details of these reports are not given here.

checks.claim: Patients with AP2S1 mutations may have higher serum calcium levels than patients with HHC1.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper does not compare serum calcium between AP2S1 patients and FHH1 patients. It reports only that there was no correlation among the different AP2S1 mutations.

checks.claim: Patients with AP2S1 mutations may have lower urinary calcium excretion than patients with HHC1.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper does not compare urinary calcium excretion between AP2S1 patients and FHH1 patients.

checks.claim: Some patients with AP2S1 mutations have had cognitive or developmental problems.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention cognitive or developmental problems. It mentions only poor weight gain.

paragraphs.text: Nesbit et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous arg15-to-cys (R15C) mutation in the AP2S1 gene in patients with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III who did not carry CASR mutations. In vitro, the mutation reduced the sensitivity of cells expressing the calcium-sensing receptor to extracellular calcium.

checks.claim: Nesbit et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous R15C mutation in the AP2S1 gene in patients with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III who did not carry CASR mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15 and consisted of four Arg15Cys
checks.explanation: Found in patients in whom CaSR mutations had been excluded, and in the FHH3 kindreds.

checks.claim: In vitro, the AP2S1 R15C mutation reduced the sensitivity of calcium-sensing receptor-expressing cells to extracellular calcium.
